title: Orchestra routing graph

schema.route_fields: if (prose predicate) · then (string step, or array = parallel batch) · dispatch (tokens role[:lens][@level], resolvable against roles; @L2 default) · next (forward edge, must name a real state) · back_to + carry (backward edge + what travels back)
schema.state_fields: question · always (duties that fire on every entry, before route matching) · routes · match ('first' default = exclusive; 'all' = every matching route fires, at most one names next)
schema.announce: Every transition is announced in chat as `flow: <from> -> <to> (<matched if>)`. A transition without an announcement is a routing defect.
schema.validate: python3 -c "import json;d=json.load(open('.cursor/skills/orchestrator/flow.json'));s=set(d['states']);bad=[(k,e) for k,v in d['states'].items() for r in v.get('routes',[]) for e in [r.get('next'),r.get('back_to')] if e and e not in s];print(bad or 'edges ok')"
schema.reentry: A back_to carry OVERRIDES the target state's entry route text and stays active until the re-entered loop completes (e.g. plan.redteam re-entry after repair re-dispatches only the repaired lens; execute.ticket-loop re-entry on findings resumes the SAME builder; gates.fast re-entry after gate-repair skips execute.wave-close's always batch).

roles.orchestrator: main session — talks to the user, dispatches everyone, adjudicates, merges, approves, owns memory

levels: Dispatch tokens carry @L1 (minimal) / @L2 (standard, default) / @L3 (deep). Each agent file defines what its levels mean — the level contract travels in the brief. Which roles fire in which state, and at what level, IS the activation model; there is no separate matrix.

state_files.docs/orchestra/STATE.md: working memory — orchestrator sole writer; pointers not content; rewritten at wave/batch closes and before deliberate stops; stamped `written-at: <timestamp> @ <git HEAD>`; working-tree file, committed only inside batch-closing commits; 120-line cap is a smoke alarm (over = you are duplicating content that has a home), never an eviction trigger; verbatim quotes only when a ruling fits one line, else pointer only — never a trimmed quote
state_files..orchestra/state.json: machine run-record (gitignored) — exact keys: gates.last_green_hash (the green commit hash; the hook denies protected pushes while it differs from HEAD), gates.reports{<hash>: report}, redteam{verdicts,rounds,run_ids}, reviews{<ticket>: verdict}, flakes[], subagent_state_path. Written by the orchestrator at the transitions marked here; read by hooks and the janitor.
state_files.docs/plans/<feature>-ledger.md: run state for one plan — always a separate file, never a section in the plan; CLOSED stamp at archive
state_files.docs/AGENT-MEMORY.md: long-term repo memory — path/topic-tagged entries; janitor drafts, orchestrator commits in the batch-closing commit; update AND prune (git is the history — no append-only markers)
state_files..orchestra/delivery.json: per-repo delivery declaration (COMMITTED, unlike the rest of .orchestra/): provider (github | azure-devops | gitlab | plain-git), protected_branches, landing (pr | direct), server_side_gate (host enforces the gate itself), deploy policy per environment, deploy_commands patterns the hook asks on. install.sh detects the provider from the remote URL; the orchestrator reads this file before any release action.

routes.if: docs/orchestra/STATE.md exists with an OPEN run
routes.then: reconcile BEFORE acting: compare its stamp to `git rev-parse HEAD`, `git status --porcelain`, `git worktree list`; on mismatch the TREE is truth — repair STATE.md first, then enter at its recorded state

routes.if: full-suite request ('run the full e2e', scheduled trigger)
non-trivial feature/change: multi-wave, multi-subsystem, a migration, or hard to reverse
small standard change: roughly 2–5 files, no migration, reversible

routes.then: answer from recon, END
answer from a primary-source check, END
one classification question to the user with a recommendation; no work starts
two-sentence design in chat; implement inline; evidence-gated DONE (command + exit code); END — no STATE.md obligation

One fresh builder in the main tree, complete self-contained brief (template: briefs.md; the chat-approved approach text serves as the ticket).
One fresh reviewer on the diff.

routes.then: dispatch the builder, then the reviewer on its diff
gatekeeper re-proof of that done_when only; PASS continues, FAIL counts as a findings round
same builder resumes with the findings; re-review
escalation builder with the full findings history

always: gates.fast set at HEAD (see gates.fast contents); record the review verdict and set gates.last_green_hash in .orchestra/state.json exactly as gates.fast does.
Rewrite STATE.md (close the run entry); memory line to docs/AGENT-MEMORY.md only if a trap was found.

routes.then: run the fast set

routes.then: open the PR with evidence (ungated)

routes.carry: the failing gate excerpt as findings

always: No product code in any design state (throwaway prototype code on a clearly-marked disposable branch is not product code).
Record every user decision verbatim, at the moment it is made.

routes.if: the codebase can answer open questions
routes.then: dispatch scouts in parallel for all of them

design.frontier.question: Are there unsettled questions only the user can decide?

routes.then: ask ALL questions whose prerequisites are settled in one round, numbered, each with a recommended answer; loop until none remain

routes.if: a question is a fact, not a decision
routes.then: route it to recon or research instead of the user
present 2–3 approaches with trade-offs and ONE recommendation

then: architect sketches 2–3 radically different interfaces in parallel

routes.if: a question only running code can answer
routes.then: throwaway prototype on a disposable branch (clearly marked, one command to run, no polish); harvest the answer; record the ruling

routes.if: design leans on an industry standard or post-cutoff API
routes.then: queue researcher (background) for the plan phase

routes.if: approach settled (winner chosen, prototype harvested, or approaches presented)
3+ rulings or more than one approach explored
routes.then: architect drafts the spec from recon + winning approach + verbatim rulings; diff its returned Rulings section against your record — any difference is a defect

routes.if: small design (fewer than ~3 rulings, one approach)
routes.then: orchestrator drafts inline and says so; self-review for placeholders, contradictions, dual-readable lines, scope creep

design.gate.question: Did the user explicitly approve the spec?
always: Approval is explicit, never inferred.

routes.then: red-team requirements spot-check on the spec vs the verbatim rulings, before presenting
commit the spec — it is the contract every later phase cites

routes.carry: the user's words, verbatim, as new rulings

plan.recon.question: Does planning need recon beyond what design already gathered?

routes.if: design recon left open questions, ticket briefs need a path-rule harvest, or design happened in a previous session
routes.then: scout maps the gaps + harvests .cursor/rules and AGENTS.md excerpts for the touched paths
carry it forward and say so in the plan

always: Version-sensitive claims cite RESEARCH.md on disk — a ticket depending on research that does not exist yet is BLOCKED-ON-RESEARCH, not guessed.

routes.then: planner drafts the ticketed plan from spec + recon + research (brief template: briefs.md); orchestrator reviews the ticket summary and diffs quoted rulings against its record

plan.redteam.question: Do all three lenses return READY?
always: Record verdicts, rounds, and run ids into .orchestra/state.json — the plan is not executable without a redteam record.

routes.then: three red-teamers in parallel, fresh context, one lens each: requirements (spec+rulings pasted) · feasibility (must name a breaking file/symbol) · scope (ownership traps, missing edges, hidden migrations, unguarded irreversibles)

routes.carry: ONLY the failed lens's findings to the planner; re-dispatch ONLY that lens after repair, fresh context

routes.then: orchestrator adjudicates: repair inline, park with the user, or NOT-READY as the honest terminal state
to the USER verbatim with a recommendation — never silently repaired

routes.if: all READY with ZERO findings on round 1 of a large or irreversible plan
routes.then: suspect the skeptics: tighten briefs (paste rulings, name the diff surface), rerun once; READY-with-minor-findings is a normal first-round outcome and is accepted
commit the plan

execute.setup.question: How many builders will edit concurrently this wave?
always: Ledger file (docs/plans/<feature>-ledger.md) exists before the first dispatch.
Never git stash while worktrees exist.

routes.then: main tree, no worktree

one worktree per builder (git worktree add <repo>/.cursor/worktrees/<ticket> -b <ticket-branch>; check you are not already inside one; .cursor/worktrees/ gitignored); install dependencies and PROVE each toolchain before dispatch; own ports per tree

routes.if: a worktree's toolchain proof fails and one repair attempt does not fix it
routes.then: collapse the wave to sequential builders in the main tree — never dispatch into a broken tree

routes.if: yes (several independent → parallel, worktree rule applies)
routes.then: fresh builder per ticket with its complete self-contained brief; ledger 'running' only after dispatch returns an id

routes.if: builder reports BLOCKED on a plan defect (missing file ownership, wrong command)
routes.carry: the defect as a planner L1 repair; other tickets keep running

routes.if: builder reports BLOCKED for another reason
routes.then: resolve or take to the user; re-dispatch

execute.review.question: What does the fresh reviewer say about this ticket's diff?
always: Builder success reports are never evidence.
Record the review verdict per ticket into .orchestra/state.json and the ledger.

routes.then: fresh reviewer with ticket + diff + builder's claimed evidence + trailer
gatekeeper re-proof: that ticket's done_when only, honest capture
ledger complete with evidence

routes.carry: findings to the SAME builder (resume; a fresh builder with the findings history counts when resume is unavailable)

routes.then: escalation builder with the full findings history
orchestrator adjudicates: fix decision inline, park in ledger as known issue, or ticket BLOCKED
to the USER verbatim with a recommendation — never into the loop

execute.integrate.question: Are the wave's ticket branches merged into the feature branch?

routes.if: lone-builder wave (work already on the feature branch)

routes.then: orchestrator merges each ticket branch into the feature branch in the main tree, ordered by blocking edges; conflicts resolved in daylight — both intents preserved, never --abort, never invented behavior
fresh builder as a findings round with both tickets pasted; its diff goes through execute.review before wave close

always: Rewrite docs/orchestra/STATE.md (stamped).

routes.if: worktrees exist or the batch spanned 2+ tickets
routes.then: janitor: directory inspection (rescue-or-remove), memory draft from the pasted ledger excerpt, process-adherence checklist (every ticket has a review verdict in state.json; no unmerged ticket branches; redteam record present); orchestrator executes removals and commits the memory draft in this batch-closing commit
orchestrator writes the memory line itself in the batch-closing commit

routes.if: first wave of the feature and the repo lands via PRs/MRs (delivery.landing != 'direct')
routes.then: open a DRAFT PR/MR now with the provider's CLI — early, cheap, never a blocker; evidence-so-far in the body

gates.fast.question: Does the fast set pass at the post-merge, post-memory HEAD?
always: The orchestrator derives or approves the file→spec mapping and pastes the exact command list — scoping is never the gatekeeper's guess.
Record the report into .orchestra/state.json under gates.reports keyed by commit hash, and on green set gates.last_green_hash to that hash — the hook reads exactly this key.
Widening is mechanical, not judgment: a diff touching dependency manifests, build/tsconfig, migrations/schema, shared types/tokens, or auth widens the scoped set.

routes.then: fast set at HEAD: lint + typecheck + scoped unit + smoke core + framework doctor (per the repo's verified tooling list, e.g. React Doctor on React repos) + scoped e2e when a user-facing flow changed (isolated port)

routes.carry: the failing gate excerpt as findings to a lone builder in the main tree; re-run the set after — skip the wave-close always-batch on gate-repair re-entry

routes.then: quarantine ledger in state.json: first occurrence → ship allowed + flake ticketed; second occurrence of the same flake → mandatory fix ticket before that surface merges again; no per-flake user question after the first

routes.if: green and the feature is complete

audit.decide.question: Does this change-set need the two-axis audit before release?

routes.if: the batch closed with 2+ tickets, or the user asks
single-ticket run (the reviewer already saw the whole diff)

audit.run.question: What do the two axes report?
always: Reports are presented verbatim, never merged — separation prevents one axis masking the other.

routes.then: auditor(standards) + auditor(spec) in parallel; small diffs pasted, large diffs passed as the pinned command + file list
to the USER verbatim

routes.carry: verified findings as a findings round; re-audit the touched surface after

routes.then: present both reports with per-axis worst-issue lines; END — no gates, no release, no push

routes.if: both CLEAN or user accepts residuals (chain run)

release.merge.question: Who gates the merge — the host (server_side_gate) or the local hash record — and can the gated hash be the shipped hash?
always: Read the repo's delivery declaration (AGENTS.md 'Delivery' line + .orchestra/delivery.json): provider, protected branches, landing rule, server_side_gate, deploy policy. Use that provider's CLI (github: gh · azure-devops: az repos · gitlab: glab · plain-git: git).

The hook floor: pushes/merges to protected branches — git, gh, az repos, glab — surface a Cursor 'ask' to the real user, and are denied while gates.last_green_hash ≠ HEAD (relaxed when server_side_gate is true, because the host builds the preview merge commit). That ask IS the merge approval.

routes.if: server_side_gate true (e.g. Azure DevOps branch policy with build validation)
routes.then: make sure the host's required checks match the fast set; mark the PR ready and set auto-complete — the platform gates and merges the preview merge commit, so the gated hash is provably the shipped hash

routes.if: no server-side gate, fast-gate green at HEAD, branch current with the target
routes.then: mark the PR ready with the final gate report; merge fast-forward so the gated hash becomes the target HEAD

routes.if: no server-side gate and the branch is behind the target
routes.then: merge the target INTO the feature branch (agent-run rebases are blocked by the guardrail), re-run the fast set, then fast-forward
merge, then auto re-run the fast set at the target HEAD (mechanical, non-approval); only that green releases a deploy

routes.if: no server-side gate and HEAD moved past the gate record (mechanical check: `git diff --stat <gate-hash>..HEAD -- ':!docs' ':!*.md'` non-empty)
routes.carry: stale-gate: re-run at current HEAD; docs/memory-only commits do NOT void a gate

routes.if: merge done and deploy policy is 'auto' for this repo/environment AND the diff contains no migrations/schema changes
merge done, deploy gated (production default, or migrations present)
routes.then: releaser stages the deploy and pauses: NEEDS-APPROVAL with exact command + blast radius; spec-axis audit must be green before a production deploy. On Azure DevOps, a Pipelines environment approval check is the natural home for this pause — say so when one exists

routes.if: merge done and no deploy is configured or in scope for this change
gated and the user approves in chat
routes.then: re-dispatch the releaser with the authorization block (USER APPROVED IN CHAT verbatim + EXECUTE EXACTLY); the hook's ask is the floor, the block is the record
verify the health check and record evidence

routes.if: health check fails, or main breaks after merge
verified, or user defers the deploy (record 'deferred:' in STATE.md — it survives the idle reset)

always: Revert first, diagnose second — restoring the last gated state is auto-executable because it restores a proven hash.

routes.then: releaser stages the revert of the merge commit; execute; verify the health check at the reverted state

routes.carry: the failure evidence as the bug to diagnose

fullsuite.run.question: User-triggered full verification — never on the critical path.
always: Never blocks a PR, a merge, or a deploy. Runs whole-codebase, on main, in a quiet worktree or a Cursor cloud agent.

routes.then: full suite; results appended to docs/orchestra/STATE.md pointers and reported
each failure becomes an intake item (bug lane), prioritized with the user

bug.feedback-loop.question: Does a named, already-run, red-capable, fast, deterministic command reproduce it?

routes.then: build one (failing test > curl > CLI diff > headless browser > bisect harness); non-deterministic → raise and state the reproduction rate first; perf → measured baseline before any change; no loop possible → stop and ask the user
minimise; 3–5 ranked falsifiable hypotheses shown to the user (non-blocking); instrument one variable at a time; fix = one ticket through the execute machinery with the regression test first

routes.if: fix verified and diff is trivial
routes.then: clean instrumentation; winning hypothesis in the commit message
close any open batch (worktrees inspected/removed, memory committed); verify zero live worktrees, ledger CLOSED, STATE.md rewritten to idle (keeping any 'deferred:' line); expired RESEARCH.md removed

quote the evidence (commands + exit codes + hashes); when a run/ledger was opened, cleanup.final must have run; standalone reviews, full-suite runs, trivial changes, and pure answers declare DONE with evidence alone
name it honestly; never dress one terminal state as another

user changes a ruling mid-run.then: record the resume point (ledger + STATE.md); settle in-flight dispatches per the ledger; architect L1 revision of the spec carrying the new ruling verbatim -> design.gate for approval; then planner Repair scoped to the affected tickets only -> plan.redteam re-dispatching ONLY the touched lenses; then re-enter execute.ticket-loop at the recorded resume point
user changes a ruling mid-run.carry: the new ruling verbatim + the recorded resume point

user interrupt during execution.then: stop dispatching; report ledger state; resume from the ledger — never re-dispatch blind (two builders on one ticket in one tree is corruption)

a dispatch errors or never returns.then: check the ledger and tree for partial commits, then dispatch fresh; liveness for background agents = state file + mtime at the verified sub-agent state path

invariants: Sub-agent briefs are self-contained: verbatim-critical excerpts (rulings, done_when, path rules) pasted; bulk material passed as pointers the agent reads itself.
Sub-agents never spawn sub-agents (policy; subagentStart hook denies it). All fan-out is the orchestrator's.
User rulings travel verbatim — full quote only when it fits one line, else pointer; never a trimmed quote.
Evidence = command + exit code (captured without pipes) or both-theme screenshots; assertions are not evidence.
Worktrees only for 2+ concurrent editors; created, integrated, and removed by the orchestrator within the wave.
Judgement roles (architect, planner, red-teamer, auditor, builder-max) run model: inherit — the ceiling; the rest are pinned lower at install (install.sh verifies).
Approval boundaries: prepare-then-pause; the hook's protected-branch 'ask' is the deterministic floor; files never authorize.
Memory lands in the batch-closing commit; stale entries are pruned, not superseded-in-place.
Honest terminal states — DONE, BLOCKED, NOT-READY, NEEDS-APPROVAL; never one dressed as another.
